Thanks Jordan — excited to move to a formal MAP. Before we lock milestones, Finance is asking for a simple token/unit economics sheet they can use in procurement. Can you send: 
- tokens/$ numbers for the pilot (per-model and an example aggregate)
- caching assumptions (prefix, KV hit-rate scenarios)

We’re aiming to close commercial terms the week of Dec 6; procurement needs the numbers now for their internal review. Looping in finance@medisync.com — they may ask for more detail.

Medisync

Kira — great, thanks. I’ve attached a draft MAP with a placeholder cost worksheet (MAP-draft-20261121.xlsx) that contains three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). High-level answers below; Ben and Karthik are cc’d for detail.

Summary (top-line):
- Baseline tokens/$ (expected): ~12,000 tokens per USD for our quantized inference profile on the model you referenced (redwood-std-1).
- Caching: prefix caching can reduce token spend by 15–40% depending on prompt reuse; we show a 25% hit baseline in the draft scenario.
- Batching: typical client batching policy (50–200ms window) yields 10–20% additional throughput without pushing p95 latency above 250ms for short requests.
- Exit criteria suggestion: pilot pass if realized tokens/$ >= 10k and average p95 latency <= 300ms under the expected traffic profile.

Ask: can you share a representative traffic sample (requests/day, average prompt length, prompt reuse %) so we can replace placeholders with your numbers? Once Ben and Karthik confirm the calc details I’ll produce a short one-pager Finance can sign off on.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Kira / team — pinging with the worked example and assumptions we used to generate Jordan’s top-line. See attached (cost-scenarios-20261122.pdf) for exported tables and sample calculations. Key assumptions called out here so Finance can map to their spreadsheet: 

1) Model and perf profile
- Model: redwood-std-1, fp16 quantized to 4-bit runtime when applicable.
- Token throughput: we assume 75,000 tokens / GPU-hour for the above profile in sustained steady state.

2) Tokens per request examples
- Short query: 60 tokens (prompt + reply)
- Medium: 280 tokens
- Long: 1,200 tokens
- Weighted average (Medisync sample estimate): 420 tokens / request

3) Caching (prefix + KV)
- Prefix reuse hit-rate: conservative 10%, expected 25%, aggressive 45%
- Effective tokens saved = hit_rate * average_prefix_tokens (we used avg prefix = 120 tokens)
- KV cache (session-level) reduces full-generation token count on repeat flows; we model an extra 5–10% savings if session reuse is present.

4) Batching
- Batch window: 50ms (default), 200ms (burst).
- Throughput improvement: 8% @50ms, 18% @200ms.
- Latency impact: p95 latency increases by ~40–70ms for short requests at 200ms window; p95 stays < 300ms in expected scenarios.

5) Token/$ derivation (expected scenario)
- GPU cost basis + infra overhead -> $0.000083 per token -> ~12,000 tokens / $1.00
- With caching (expected 25%): effective tokens/$ ~16,000
- With batching gains applied to shared infra cost we show an effective tokens/$ uplift of ~12–18% depending on window.

If you prefer, we can produce a single-cell metric that Finance can plug into their procurement model (e.g., median tokens_per_dollar = 15,200 for expected).

Notes and caveats: these numbers are workload-dependent. If Medisync has many long-context requests or low prefix reuse, realized tokens/$ will drop. We highlight gating checks in the MAP one-pager.

Attachment: cost-scenarios-20261122.pdf (application/pdf)

Kira / team — thanks for the clarifying questions. We validated the assumptions against a small Medisync sample you shared in the call; below is the agreed language I propose for the MAP one-pager (I attached MAP-final-20261125.xlsx):

Agreed cost assumptions (conservative gating scenario):
- Conservative tokens/$: 10,000 tokens per USD (this is the single conservative metric Finance requested).
- Conservative caching: 10% prefix hit (conservative), avg prefix = 120 tokens (includes system + user prompt).
- Batching baseline: 50ms window for production; if customer elects 200ms window for throughput tests we will measure p95 delta during the pilot.

Measured/expected impacts (expected scenario):
- Expected tokens/$ (after expected caching 25%): ~15,000 tokens per USD.
- Batching uplift: expected +12% tokens/$ at the 50ms window for aggregate traffic mix.

MAP exit criteria (pilot pass/fail):
- Pass: realized tokens/$ >= 10,000 AND average p95 latency <= 300ms during a 48-hour stress window that matches the MAP traffic profile.
- Fail: realized tokens/$ < 10,000 OR sustained p95 latency > 300ms under stress. If fail, MAP includes an additional 2-week optimization iteration (tuning batching/caching and model/config adjustments).

Milestones & timeline (proposal):
- 2026-11-26: MAP one-pager signed off (this doc + MAP-final-20261125.xlsx).
- 2026-11-29: Pilot environment provisioned (Private/Dedicated selection) and telemetry hooks enabled.
- 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-08: 48-hour pilot stress window and acceptance test.
- 2026-12-09: MAP results review; commercial close to follow if pass.

Next steps: please confirm sign-off on the conservative tokens/$ = 10,000 and we’ll push the MAP to signatures. I added HubSpot link for the deal and a Drive folder with the final MAP.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
